source_refs.note: Mode of Sulfonamides Action:: a main subheading of 23.2.4 Sulfonamides, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 212-212.

items: Bacteriostatic Effect: Sulfonamides do not kill bacteria immediately but inhibit their growth, allowing the body's immune system to destroy them.

Selective Toxicity: Sulfonamides are selectively toxic to bacteria because of how they handle folate. Bacteria must build this essential vitamin from scratch, whereas humans simply absorb it from food. This allows the drug to starve the bacteria of vital nutrients while leaving human cells untouched."
Competitive Inhibition: Sulfonamides bind to the enzyme responsible for creating folate, essentially taking para amino benzoic acid pathway (Folate metabolism).
Combined Therapy: They are often combined with other agents, like trimethoprim, to create a stronger bactericidal effect (killing bacteria).
Broad Spectrum: They are effective against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, often used for urinary tract infections, acne, and respiratory infections.
